particledrawing.command.batch.usage: Usage: /pdraw particle batch <name> kind=<emitter|shape|program> key=value...; use /pdraw particle batch help [group] for all keys.
particledrawing.command.batch.examples:
Examples:
/pdraw particle batch ring kind=emitter anchor=fixed anchor.pos=~ ~4 ~ sample.count=1 orbit="vec3(cos(t*0.0025)*4,0,sin(t*0.0025)*4)" appearance.style=soft_dot appearance.color=#b060ff motion.vy=-0.03 emitter.lifetime=60 rate=2 mode=start
/pdraw particle batch spark kind=sphere center=~ ~1 ~ radius=2 count=200 appearance.color=#ff4040 particle.lifetime=30
/pdraw particle batch rune kind=program program.1=delay,20 program.2=fade_in,30,ease_out program.3=move,0,3,0,40

command.help.overview.body: ParticleDrawing: the server declares particles, the client evaluates and renders them locally every tick. Pick a topic; click a green example to put it in the chat box.
command.help.particle.body: Three carriers: one-shot particles (shape + look, drawn once), named groups (fixed members, good for timelines, morphs and programs), and emitters (sampling + formulas, continuously spawned). Groups and emitters only send a declaration; the client simulates and renders locally.
command.help.emitter.body: Emitter = anchor + sampling + formulas + emission cadence + look. sample provides seeds, birth sets spawn position/velocity/color, motion changes velocity per tick, let defines per-particle constants and orbit moves the whole anchor. burst walks the samples once; start keeps emitting. emitter.lifetime is particle lifetime; use emit_from / emit_until for the emission window. Keep burst sample count within rate (max 1024), otherwise samples are born over several ticks.
command.help.batch.body: One command writes one setup: kind=emitter for emitters, kind=<shape> for one-shot groups and kind=program for group timelines. Keys map one-to-one to the long-form subcommands; validation happens before anything is applied. Positions using ~ follow the execution position. Open the batch key catalog to page through every key.
command.help.animation.body: Play .pdrawc animations exported by the editor, control playback, cameras, variables and diagnostics. Animation files live in <game dir>/animations/ and are synced by the server.
command.help.camera.body: The free camera sends a target pose to the player and the client interpolates towards it every frame. smooth is the approach rate per second (default 12); fov overrides the field of view.
command.help.texture.body: texture reload hot-reloads custom textures. particle:<namespace>:<name> reads a particle frame sequence from the resource pack: finite lifetimes pick frames by age, infinite lifetimes loop; #frame pins one frame and @fps sets an explicit animation rate.
command.help.light.body: light prints dynamic-light diagnostics on the client: light source count, version, and the light level under and in front of the player. Use it first when particles do not seem to light the world.
command.help.examples.body: Examples live in examples/: examples/commands compares long-form and batch commands; examples/showcase has the five star-temple effects. Paths shown in help can be clicked to copy.
command.batch.help.title: Batch command help
command.batch.help.overview: One command writes an emitter, a one-shot group or a group timeline; keys map one-to-one to the long-form subcommands. Use the buttons below to page or jump.
command.batch.help.list_hint: Click a key name for details.
command.batch.help.hover: applies to %1$s · group %2$s · click for details
command.batch.help.empty: No keys shown in this group: %1$s
command.batch.help.unknown: No such key or help entry: %1$s
command.batch.group.top: Top-level keys: kind is required, mode decides how an emitter starts, keep appends to a timeline and dryrun validates without applying.
command.batch.group.anchor: Anchor: fixed in place, entity-following, or shared with another emitter; coordinates accept ~ and ^.
command.batch.group.sampling: Sampling: count samples the parameter uniformly, range walks by step, grid takes a spatial grid; image / mesh / text take points from images, mesh surfaces or glyphs.
command.batch.group.formula: Formulas: let is a per-particle constant, birth is evaluated at spawn, motion every tick, where filters seeds, kill decides removal and orbit moves the whole anchor. Quote formulas.
command.batch.group.runtime: Runtime values: variable declares values programs can read; state stores values kept across ticks.
command.batch.group.emitter: Emitter runtime keys: particle lifetime, emission window, rate, alive cap, spacing, simulation range and follow. rate is at most 1024 per tick.
command.batch.group.collision: Collision: particles can collide with blocks, liquids or entities; bounce and friction tune the response.
command.batch.group.subemit: Sub-emit: spawn a child particle when a particle dies, with count, lifetime, velocity and scale controls.
command.batch.group.unset: Unset: reset a whole section or a single field to its default.
command.batch.group.shape: Shape parameters: different one-shot shapes require different size and position fields such as radius, height and count.
command.batch.group.particle: One-shot particle keys: lifetime, spawn velocity, forces, stagger, facing, hollow and taper; same as the particle add keys.
command.batch.group.text: Text: kind=text content, glyph height, point count and font; | starts a new line.
command.batch.group.program: Group timeline: program.N appends actions by index (move / spin / fade / morph ...); keep=true appends to an existing timeline.
command.batch.group.morph: Morph: morph.slots gives a world-space target position formula for each particle; morph.ticks / easing / path / wobble shape the transition.
command.batch.group.appearance: Appearance: texture, size, glowing, additive, dynamic light, stretching, trails, models and depth fade, matching the particle add appearance keys.
